findings.reason: the write-path declaration is a claim about the files the node may touch, and without `reckon/mcp.py` the declared entry point cannot be built at the declared scope; §42 must add `reckon/mcp.py` (the `_crew` parameter and its forward to `serve_crew_view`) and its done-when should exercise the tool's call, or drop that entry point from the sentence.
findings.text: the "refresh ... reachable three ways" sentence makes the MCP entry point a name-read off `CrewArgs`, but `_crew` in `reckon/mcp.py:1936` declares the tool's real parameters and `reckon/mcp.py:2166` forwards each one by name to `serve_crew_view`; `CrewArgs` (reckon/_mcp_tools.py:83) is referenced only by tests, so a node confined to §42's declared write paths cannot make `crew(view="models", refresh=True)` recompute anything, and its gate — which drives `serve_crew_view` directly — would still pass while the MCP surface silently ignores the flag

findings.reason: dispatch's live-claim check refuses on the files actually held, so a node dispatched on this line's claim is held by a node the plan never named; the paragraph must name the holder nodes §42's three files actually have.
findings.text: the paragraph states "Crew-surface §7's repair-and-check node holds three of these files: `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md` and `tests/test_skill_contracts.py`", but the crew-surface plan's node table (docs/plans/the-crew-surface-is-one-tool-and-a-few-verbs.html:243) gives `cso-repair-and-check-families-fold` only `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py`, `reckon/crew/obligations.py`, `reckon/crew/prompts.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py` and `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md` — one of the three named; `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` and `tests/test_skill_contracts.py` are held by §7's other nodes (budget-family-folds, watch-family-folds) and by §8's tombstone nodes (`cso-list-retires`, `cso-ledger-and-velocity-retire`, `cso-crew-view-filters-live-runs`), so a dispatcher reading this line waits on the wrong node and the stated ordering agreement binds the wrong holder

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the new anchors resolve: reckon/crew_run_commands.py:304 is `@crew.command(name="view")`, the ack verb is at crew_run_commands.py:1522, CrewArgs is at reckon/_mcp_tools.py:83, CREW_VIEWS at reckon/mcp_views.py:3598, serve_crew_view at reckon/mcp_views.py:3626, and tests/test_crew_view_serves_every_view.py, tests/test_skill_contracts.py and test_ship_crew_views_match_the_typed_mcp_surface (tests/test_skill_contracts.py:1165) all exist.

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate logs and the evidence fragment sit in the run directory, not in a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed lines carry no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §42 names "an optional `refresh` field on `CrewArgs` (`reckon/_mcp_tools.py`)" as one of the three ways `refresh` is reached, but the MCP surface's runtime parameter list is `_crew(...)` in `reckon/mcp.py`, which forwards an explicit named argument to `serve_crew_view`; `CrewArgs` is a pydantic schema the runtime handler never reads (it is referenced only by tests), so the field alone makes `refresh` unreachable through the surface `coordinator-surface=mcp` names, and the file that carries that caller is outside §42's written paths.
